extracted.intended_audience: microbiologists, prokaryote taxonomists, authors describing new prokaryotic taxa, and nomenclature committees (ICSP/Judicial Commission)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules, principles and recommendations governing formation, publication, typification, and stability of scientific names of prokaryotes (ICNP / Prokaryotic Code) for authors, editors and nomenclature bodies.

rubrics_metrics.name: General Consideration 1
rubrics_metrics.description: The progress of bacteriology can be furthered by a precise system of nomenclature accepted by the majority of bacteriologists of all nations.

rubrics_metrics.name: General Consideration 2
rubrics_metrics.description: To achieve order in nomenclature, it is essential that scientific names be regulated by internationally accepted Rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: General Consideration 3
rubrics_metrics.description: The Rules which govern the scientific nomenclature used in the biological sciences are embodied in International Codes of Nomenclature (see Appendix 1 for a list of these Codes).

rubrics_metrics.name: General Consideration 4
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules of nomenclature do not govern the delimitation of taxa nor determine their relations. The Rules are primarily for assessing the correctness of the names applied to defined taxa; they also prescribe the procedures for creating and proposing new names.

rubrics_metrics.name: General Consideration 5
rubrics_metrics.description: This Code of Nomenclature of Prokaryotes applies to all Prokaryotes. The nomenclature of eukaryotic microbial groups is provided for by other Codes: fungi and algae by the International Code of Nomenclature for algae, fungi and plants, protozoa by the International Code of Zoological Nomenclature. The nomenclature of viruses is provided for by the International Code of Virus Classification and Nomenclature (see Appendix 1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note lists alternative names/categories covered by other Codes; contains note giving examples of groups referred to as 'Prokaryotes'.

rubrics_metrics.name: General Consideration 6
rubrics_metrics.description: This Code is divided into Principles, Rules, and Recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (1) The Principles (Chapter 2) form the basis of the Code, and the Rules and Recommendations are derived from them. (2) The Rules (Chapter 3) are designed to make effective the Principles, to put the nomenclature of the past in order, and to provide for the nomenclature of the future. (3) The Recommendations (Chapter 3) deal with subsidiary points and are appended to the Rules which they supplement. Recommendations do not have the force of Rules; they are intended to be guides to desirable practice in the future. (4) Provisions for emendations, exceptions and interpretation are made by the ICSP and its Judicial Commission. (5) Appendices assist application. (6) Index references Definitions in boldface.

rubrics_metrics.name: General Consideration 7
rubrics_metrics.description: Nomenclature deals with the following: terms used to denote taxonomic categories; relative rank of categories; names applied to individual taxa.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples provided (e.g., species: Pseudomonas aeruginosa; genus: Pseudomonas; family: Pseudomonadaceae).

rubrics_metrics.name: General Consideration 8
rubrics_metrics.description: The International Code of Nomenclature of Prokaryotes is an instrument of scientific communication. Names have meaning only in the context in which they were formed and used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial note: examples in earlier revisions updated to reflect names with current standing; explanation of rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle 1
rubrics_metrics.description: The essential points in nomenclature are as follows: 1. Aim at stability of names. 2. Avoid or reject the use of names which may cause error or confusion. 3. Avoid the useless creation of names. 4. Nothing in this Code may be construed to restrict the freedom of taxonomic thought or action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: 'Name' refers to scientific names applied to prokaryotes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle 2
rubrics_metrics.description: The nomenclature of prokaryotes is not independent of botanical and zoological nomenclature. When naming new taxa in the rank of genus or higher, due consideration is to be given to avoiding names which are regulated by the International Code of Zoological Nomenclature and the International Code of Nomenclature for algae, fungi and plants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: lists resources maintaining zoological/botanical names (Zoological Record, Index Nominum Genericorum, etc.); change effective from ICSP acceptance (Nov 2000) and not retroactive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle 3
rubrics_metrics.description: The scientific names of all taxa are Latin or latinized words treated as Latin regardless of their origin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation to consult Chapter 3 Section 9 and Appendix 9 for formation guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle 4
rubrics_metrics.description: The primary purpose of giving a name to a taxon is to supply a means of referring to it rather than to indicate the characters or the history of the taxon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle 5
rubrics_metrics.description: The application of the names of taxa is determined by means of nomenclatural types, referred to in this Code as types.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Chapter 3, Section 4 for rules on types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle 6
rubrics_metrics.description: The correct name of a taxon is based upon valid publication, legitimacy, and priority of publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Chapter 3, Section 5 for details on validity, legitimacy and priority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle 7
rubrics_metrics.description: A name of a taxon has no status under the Rules and no claim to recognition unless it is validly published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-reference to rules on valid publication in Chapter 3 Section 5.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle 8
rubrics_metrics.description: Each order or taxon of a lower rank with a given circumscription, position, and rank can bear only one correct name, i.e., the earliest that is in accordance with the Rules of this Code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provision for exceptions is made (see Rules 23a, 23b and ICSP Statutes). Notes define 'circumscription', 'position', and 'rank'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle 9
rubrics_metrics.description: The name of a taxon should not be changed without sufficient reason based either on further taxonomic studies or on the necessity of giving up a nomenclature that is contrary to the Rules of this Code.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 1a
rubrics_metrics.description: This revision of the International Code of Nomenclature of Bacteria supersedes all previous revisions of the Bacteriological Code and shall be known as the International Code of Nomenclature of Prokaryotes (Prokaryotic Code (2008 Revision)). It will apply from the date of publication (2016).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 1b
rubrics_metrics.description: Alterations to this Code can only be made by the ICSP at one of its plenary sessions. Proposals for modifications should be made in sufficient time to allow publication in the IJSEM before the next International Congress of Bacteriology and Applied Microbiology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See the Statutes of the ICSP for further provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 2
rubrics_metrics.description: The Rules of this Code are retroactive, except where exceptions are specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of exceptions cited (Rule 18a, Rule 30).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 3
rubrics_metrics.description: Names contrary to a Rule cannot be maintained, except that the ICSP, on recommendation of the Judicial Commission, may make exceptions to the Rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-reference: Rule 23a and ICSP Statutes for exception process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 4
rubrics_metrics.description: In the absence of a relevant Rule or where the consequences of a Rule are uncertain, a summary in which all pertinent facts are outlined should be submitted to the Judicial Commission for consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Appendix 8 for preparation of a Request for an Opinion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 5a
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions of the taxonomic categories will inevitably vary with individual opinion, but the relative order of these categories may not be altered in any classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 5b
rubrics_metrics.description: The taxonomic categories above and including species which are covered by these Rules are given below in ascending taxonomic rank. Those in the left-hand column should be recognized where pertinent; those in the right-hand column are optional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List of ranks provided (species, genus, subgenus, subtribe, tribe, subfamily, family, order, suborder, subclass, class) and Latin equivalents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 5c
rubrics_metrics.description: A species may be divided into subspecies, which are dealt with by the Rules of this Code (see Rules 13a–d). Variety is a synonym of subspecies; its use is not encouraged and after publication of this Code the use of the term variety for new names will have no standing in nomenclature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 5d
rubrics_metrics.description: Taxa below the rank of subspecies (infrasubspecific subdivisions) are not covered by the Rules of this Code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Rule 14a and Appendix 10 for advice on infrasubspecific designations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 6
rubrics_metrics.description: The scientific names of all taxa must be treated as Latin; names of taxa above the rank of species are single words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation 6 provides detailed advice on forming new prokaryotic names and epithets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation 6
rubrics_metrics.description: Advisory guidance for forming new names and epithets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (1) Avoid names or epithets that are very long or difficult to pronounce. (2) Make names agreeable and easy to pronounce when latinized. (3) Avoid words from other languages if Latin/Greek equivalents exist; exceptions for local items with no Latin/Greek (foods, places). (4) Do not adopt unpublished names found in authors' notes unless approved. (5) Give etymology of new generic names and epithets. (6) Determine proposed name is in accordance with the Rules. (7) Maintain Greek K and Z and Medieval Latin J to avoid confusion (examples). (8) Use M.L. for Medieval Latin and N.L. for Neo-Latin. (9) Indicate arbitrary names and make them easy to spell/pronounce. (10) Authors should not name organisms after themselves; if derived from personal names, use only untruncated family name (rarely first).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 7
rubrics_metrics.description: The name of a taxon above the rank of genus up to and including order is a substantive or an adjective used as a substantive of Latin or Greek origin. It is in the feminine gender, the plural number, and written with an initial capital letter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Family Pseudomonadaceae. Historical notes about forms qualifying 'plantae' and 'procaryotae'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 8
rubrics_metrics.description: The name of each taxon (covered by the Code) above the rank of order is a Latin or latinized word. The name of a class is in the neuter gender, the plural number and written with an initial capital letter. The name is formed by the addition of the suffix –ia to the stem of the name of the type genus of the type order of the class. The name of a subclass is in the feminine gender, the plural number and written with an initial capital letter; formed by addition of suffix –idae.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Kingdom—Procaryotae; Class—Clostridia.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 9
rubrics_metrics.description: The name of a taxon between subclass and genus is formed by the addition of the appropriate suffix to the stem of the name of the type genus (see Rule 15). These suffixes are presented in Table 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table 1 gives suffixes for ranks (e.g., -ales for order, -aceae for family, -oideae for subfamily, -eae for tribe, -inae for subtribe).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 10a
rubrics_metrics.description: The name of a genus or subgenus is a substantive, or an adjective used as a substantive, in the singular number and written with an initial capital letter. The name may be taken from any source and may even be composed in an arbitrary manner. It is treated as a Latin substantive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Clostridium, Haemophilus, Spirillum, Lactobacillus, Flavobacterium, Shigella, Afipia, Desemzia, Waddlia, Cedecea.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation 10a
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendations for forming new generic or subgeneric names.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (1) Refrain from naming genera/subgenera after persons unconnected with bacteriology or natural science. (2) Give a feminine form to all personal generic/subgeneric names commemorating persons. (3) Avoid introducing names already in use in botany or zoology, particularly well-known names.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 10b
rubrics_metrics.description: Generic and subgeneric names are subject to the same Rules and Recommendations, except that Rule 10c applies only to subgeneric names.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 10c
rubrics_metrics.description: The name of a subgenus, when included with the name of a species, is placed in parentheses along with the abbreviation 'subgen.' between the generic name and specific epithet. When included, the citation should be inserted before closure of the parentheses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Moraxella (subgen. Moraxella Lwoff 1939, 173) lacunata; Moraxella (subgen. Branhamella Catlin 1970, 157) catarrhalis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 11
rubrics_metrics.description: The taxonomic categories section, subsection, series, and subseries are informal categories not regulated by the Rules of this Code. Their designations do not compete with the names of genera and subgenera as to priority and homonymy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note explaining priority (first published name is correct) and homonymy (same name for different taxa; earlier homonym = senior homonym, later homonym = junior homonym).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 12a
rubrics_metrics.description: The name of a species is a binary combination consisting of the name of the genus followed by a single specific epithet. If a specific epithet is formed from two or more words, then the words are to be joined. If the words were not joined in the effective publication, then the epithet is not to be rejected but the form is to be corrected by joining the words, which can be done by any author. If an epithet has been hyphenated, its parts should be joined. The name is considered to have been validly published and retains its standing in nomenclature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of corrected epithets: Nocardia otitidis-caviarum → Nocardia otitidiscaviarum; Propionibacterium acidi-propionici → Propionibacterium acidipropionici.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 12b
rubrics_metrics.description: No specific or subspecific epithets within the same genus may be the same if based on different types.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Two different Corynebacterium names based on different types cannot share the same specific epithet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 12c
rubrics_metrics.description: A specific epithet may be taken from any source and may even be composed arbitrarily. A specific epithet must be treated in one of three ways: (1) as an adjective that must agree in gender with the generic name; (2) as a substantive (noun) in apposition in the nominative case; (3) as a substantive (noun) in the genitive case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: aureus in Staphylococcus aureus (adjective); Desulfovibrio gigas (apposition); coli in Escherichia coli (genitive).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation 12c
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendations when forming specific epithets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (1) Choose an epithet that indicates a property or source of the species. (2) Avoid epithets expressing a character common to all/nearly all species of a genus. (3) If from a person's name, ensure it recalls someone connected with the organism and has appropriate gender. (4) Avoid very similar epithets within the same genus. (5) Avoid using genitive and adjectival forms of the same epithet for different species in the same genus. (6) Ordinal adjectives for enumeration may include numbers up to ten (e.g., primus, secundus).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 13a
rubrics_metrics.description: The name of a subspecies is a ternary combination consisting of the name of a genus followed by a specific epithet, the abbreviation 'subsp.' (subspecies), and finally the subspecific epithet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Bacillus subtilis subsp. spizizenii Nakamura et al. 1999.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 13b
rubrics_metrics.description: A subspecific epithet is formed in the same way as a specific epithet. When adjectival in form, it agrees in gender with the generic name.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 13c
rubrics_metrics.description: No two subspecies within the same species or within the same genus may bear the same subspecific epithet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See also Rules 12b and 40d for related provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 13d
rubrics_metrics.description: A subspecies that includes the type of the species must bear the same epithet as the species.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See also Rules 40d and 45.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 14a
rubrics_metrics.description: The designations of the various taxa below the rank of subspecies are not subject to the Rules and Recommendations of this Code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For advice on their nomenclature, see Appendix 10.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 14b
rubrics_metrics.description: A Latin or latinized infrasubspecific designation may be elevated by a subsequent author to the status of a subspecies or species name providing that the resulting name is in conformity with the Rules. If so elevated, it ranks for purposes of priority from its date of elevation and is attributed to the author by whom it was elevated, provided that the author who elevates it observes Rule 27.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example provided (elevation of Pseudomonas cannabina).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 15
rubrics_metrics.description: A taxon consists of one or more elements. For each named taxon of the various taxonomic categories there shall be designated a nomenclatural type. The nomenclatural type (type) is that element of the taxon with which the name is permanently associated, whether as a correct name or as a later heterotypic synonym. The nomenclatural type is not necessarily the most typical or representative element of the taxon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Types are dealt with in Rules 16–22. Table 2 presents types for categories (e.g., species type = designated strain; genus type = designated species; family type = genus on whose name the higher taxon is based).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 16
rubrics_metrics.description: After the date of publication of this Code, the type of a taxon must be designated by the author at the time the name of the taxon is published in the IJSEM.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes: Authors intending to publish name in IJSEM with reference to a previous effectively published description under Rule 27(2) are advised also to designate the type when publishing that description. If a previous effective publication does not designate a type, the type must be designated at valid publication in IJSEM.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 17
rubrics_metrics.description: The type determines the application of the name of a taxon if the taxon is subsequently divided or united with another taxon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: division of Bacillus into Bacillus and Paenibacillus — the genus containing the type species Bacillus subtilis must retain the name Bacillus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 18a
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever possible, the type of a species or subspecies is a designated strain. The type strain is made up of living cultures descended from a strain designated as the nomenclatural type; the strain should have been maintained in pure culture and should agree closely to its characters with those in the original description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (1) Until 31 December 2000, for species not maintained in cultures a description, preserved specimen or illustration could serve as type. (2) From 1 January 2001, a description, preserved (non-viable) specimen or illustration may not serve as the type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 18b (Designation by original author)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the author in the effective publication of the name of a species or subspecies definitely designated a type strain, then this strain shall be accepted as the type strain and may be referred to as the holotype.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 18c (Designation as neotype)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a strain on which the original description was based cannot be found, a neotype strain may be proposed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A proposed neotype must be proposed in the IJSEM with citation of author(s), a description or reference to an effectively published description, and a record of permanently established culture collections where the strain is deposited. The author should show a careful search for original strains and demonstrate the proposed neotype agrees closely with the original description. The neotype becomes established two years after publication in IJSEM provided there are no objections (objections must be referred within the first year to the Judicial Commission). Note: 'strain' refers to culture or subcultures knowingly derived from the original strain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 18d (Suggested neotype)
rubrics_metrics.description: A strain suggested as a neotype but not formally proposed in accordance with Rule 18c (suggested neotype) has no standing in nomenclature until formally proposed and established.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 18e
rubrics_metrics.description: If an original strain that should constitute the type of a species is discovered subsequent to the formal proposal or establishment of a neotype for that species, the matter shall be referred immediately to the Judicial Commission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 18f
rubrics_metrics.description: If a description or illustration constitutes, or a dead preserved specimen has been designated the type of a species (Rule 18a(1)) and later a strain of this species is cultivated, then the type strain may be designated by the person who isolated the strain or by a subsequent author. This type strain shall then replace the description, illustration or preserved specimen as the nomenclatural type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The designation of a type strain in this manner must be published in the IJSEM, with authorship and date of priority determined by the effective and valid publication of the name by the original authors (Rule 24b).

rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text truncated in source; rule exists addressing cases where type/neotype strain becomes unsuitable due to changes (requires referral to subsequent rules/process).
